# `identity-operation`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports an operation whose literal operand fixes the result, such as `x * 0`, `x
& 0`, or an integer `x % 1`, and an assignment such as `x += 0` or `x *= 1` that
changes nothing.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

When one literal operand decides the result, the other operand stops
mattering: `x * 0` and `x & 0` are always `0`, an integer `x % 1` or
`@mod(x, 1)` is always `0`, and `x += 0`, `x -= 0`, `x *= 1`, `x /= 1`,
`x |= 0`, `x ^= 0`, `x <<= 0` and `x >>= 0` leave `x` as it was. Code rarely
means that. Usually a constant is stale (a scale factor or mask set to zero
while debugging), an operand was swapped, or the wrong variable was written,
and the expression silently produces a constant or does nothing.

## When it fires

It reports `*`, `*%`, `*|` and `&` with a `0` operand, `%`, `@mod` and `@rem`
with a divisor of `1` when the dividend is proven an integer (for a float they
keep the fraction), the matching compound assignments (`*= 0`, `&= 0`,
`%= 1`), and the compound assignments that change nothing. Only the plain
literals `0` and `1` count, so `@as(u32, 0) * x` is not reported. A
multiplication by `0` whose other operand is proven a float is skipped, since
infinities and NaN do not become `0`.

It stays quiet when both operands are literals (`0 * 16`) and when the same
operator with another literal appears within two lines, as in table rows and
unrolled steps (`base * 0`, `base * 1`, `base * 2`). For the same reason a
binary `x + 0`, `x - 0`, `x * 1`, `x | 0` or `x << 0` is never reported: real
code writes those beside `x + 1` and `x << 8` to keep a sequence regular.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn area(width: u32, height: u32) u32 {
    return width * height * 0;
}
```
